verses.text: The heavens, the earth, and everything in them were all finished.
By the seventh day, God had completed his work. So he rested from everything he had made.
God blessed the seventh day and set it apart, because he rested from all his work of creating.
This is how the heavens and the earth began when they were created, when Yahweh God made the earth and the sky.
No field plant had sprouted yet, and no crop was growing, because Yahweh God had not sent rain and no one was there to work the soil.
But water rose from the earth like a mist and watered the whole surface of the ground.
Yahweh God shaped the human from the soil and breathed life's breath into his nostrils. The human became a living being.
Yahweh God planted a garden in Eden, toward the east, and placed there the human he had formed.
Yahweh God made every kind of tree grow from the ground—trees beautiful to look at and good for food. In the garden's middle stood the tree of life and the tree that gives knowledge of good and evil.
A river flowed out from Eden to water the garden. From there it split into four rivers.
The first river is called Pishon. It winds through the whole land of Havilah, where there's gold.
The gold there is good, and bdellium resin and onyx stone are there too.
The second river is called Gihon. It winds through the whole land of Cush.
The third river is Hiddekel; it flows east of Assyria. The fourth is the Euphrates.
Yahweh God took the human and settled him in the garden of Eden to work it and care for it.
Yahweh God told the human, "You can eat freely from every tree in the garden,
but don't eat from the tree that gives knowledge of good and evil. The day you eat from it, you will certainly die."
Yahweh God said, "It's not good for the human to be alone. I'll make a partner who truly fits him."
Yahweh God formed every wild animal and every bird from the ground, then brought them to the human to see what he would call them. Whatever he called each living creature became its name.
The human named all the livestock, the birds in the sky, and the wild animals. But he still had no partner who truly fit him.
Yahweh God made the human fall into a deep sleep. While he slept, God took one of his ribs and closed up the flesh where it had been.
Yahweh God shaped a woman from the rib he had taken from the human and brought her to him.
The human said, "Finally—bone from my bones, flesh from my flesh! She'll be called Woman, because she was taken out of Man."
That's why a man leaves his father and mother, stays close to his wife, and the two become one flesh.
The man and his wife were both naked, and they felt no shame.
